neighbours.label: the ' j' piece that opens a split low-frequency verb (jolt, juggle, jostle, jettison), not a single-token verb of the same meaning
fire: The alarm went off at five and the noise jolted the whole household awake.
She has learned to juggle three part-time jobs and a night class.
Commuters jostle for space on the platform every morning before seven.
The captain decided to jettison the deck cargo before the storm hit.
Someone had jumbled the index cards, so the talk made no sense.
Nerves gave him the jitters before every recital at the conservatory.
Two granite slabs jut out over the valley and make a natural platform.
She spent the year juggling a thesis and a newborn.

short: ' j' piece opening a split verb
notes: Card: ' j' x4, ' en' x3, ' se' x2, ' to' x5 among peaks.
